results.reason: Part 1 states that the 10-Business-Day window expired, citing the October 13 letter. It explains that under §5.7(c) the Ferrovane non-renewal is deemed cured for Article IX and the §7.2(a) bring-down condition, and that Buyer has lost its walk right and its indemnity.

Part 3 identifies that Escrow §1.1 defines Losses as actual out-of-pocket losses, excluding diminution in value, lost profits and attorneys' fees, and that §4.3 limits disbursements to those Losses. It explains that SPA §11.11 makes the Escrow Agreement control disbursement mechanics, which limits Buyer's escrow recovery.

Part 2 covers the MSA §14.2 trigger at more than 50% of voting equity and the prior written consent requirement, and notes the 100% sale triggers it. It shows Tavinor is not in Annex 7.2(d), §5.3 or §7.2(d), notes the §4.4 rep issue, and explains the sole-source termination and repricing risk.
The memo states the window closed Monday, September 28, 2026, ten Business Days after September 14, 2026, and more than two weeks before the October 13 letter.
The memo states the escrow amount as $4,850,000.
It is a memorandum addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has 'Where it appears', 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Part 6 is an 'Open Points' table listing items that cannot be resolved from the documents and that need client input.
The memo expressly states that Harrowgate no longer has a termination right for the Ferrovane matter. Its MAE argument is framed only as leverage, not as a live termination right.
The memo expressly states that Tavinor is not listed in Annex 7.2(d) and is not a closing condition.
